output: For the actual handoff envelope, every assigned first neighbour of a high decoration is cubic and has two non-centre incidences. Classify each by whether it stays inside the support or enters a component outside it. The outside-incidence set can be empty. A positive arm uses one non-centre incidence only if its first edge is distinct from ha; the literal envelope permits a positive arm [a,h] when h lies in the core, so no such use follows from positive length alone. The existing local Type B incidence count applies to cubic-closed neighbours only. This is an inventory, not a return or payoff.

evidence.locator: two-incidence observable, zero-outside case, prior-use comparison
complete window-history post-[144] ledger and one handoff witness
prior Type B local use and strict-surplus boundary

first_missing_inference: The public handoff gives no positive number of outside incidences and no map from the full original source pattern to the one envelope’s first neighbours or complement components.
immediate_subobligations: Test the zero-outside-incidence case and the positive-outside-incidence case separately when selecting a structural tension.
For a positive arm, retain the first-edge-equals-ha exception unless a nonbacktracking invariant is proved from the literal ledger.
For any proposed use of bridgelessness, first prove an actual leaving edge and track its return on the same selected graph.

ingredients: degree-three first neighbours of high decorations
two non-centre incidences at each such neighbour

interaction.relation: Each non-centre incidence is internal to the envelope support or leads to a component of its complement; the number and source-pair incidence of the latter are unresolved.
interaction.known: The high-centre normal form makes each assigned first neighbour cubic. Arms can have zero or positive length, and the retained handoff does not require a positive arm to start with an edge distinct from ha.
interaction.unresolved: Whether any outside incidence exists, where its component attaches, whether the first arm edge is distinct from ha, and whether the rest of the source pattern uses those attachments.
interaction.domains: one selected graph G and one handoff witness; no replacement graph or identified class-audit existential
interaction.previous_use: The Type B local ledger counts non-centre incidences by window location only for cubic-closed neighbours in the assigned support. [144] makes assigned neighbours cubic, not necessarily cubic-closed, and routes only two selected source pairs to one envelope.

side_observations: If every relevant incidence remains inside the support, the proposed outside-return mechanism has no input.
